minutes.headline: Planning Board endorsed an ANR at 68 Laurel Lane, approved a Lunenburg Central sign modification, and continued the 1325 Mass Ave hearing to January 23.
minutes.summary: The board endorsed an approval-not-required plan, then approved a modification to the Lunenburg Central site plan for signage. The long 1325 Mass Ave site plan and stormwater hearing drew sharp abutter objections about a contractor yard building. It was continued to await peer review and other board outcomes. The Select Board chair also presented municipal building concepts, with no vote and a return in two weeks.

public_comment.topic: Opposition to the 240-foot contractor storage building: operating hours, noise, property values, oversight, building size, request for an artist rendering, earth removal, and runoff in the water supply district.
Resident of Townsend Harbor Road objected to the rear building as industrial in size, raised traffic near the schools, asked for shorter noise hours and a downsized building.
Asked for an artist rendering showing how the whole project would look from the road.

budget_items.topic: TC Passios building renovation vs. new build
budget_items.what_was_said: Early estimates for renovating versus tearing down and rebuilding were described as very large, and voters were not expected to back the higher one.
Rehabilitation space was estimated at a per-square-foot rate that reaches the millions quickly for the after-school programs' space.
A new town hall add-on to the Ritter building would be limited new construction.

budget_items.topic: Stormwater basin capacity at 1325 Mass Ave
budget_items.what_was_said: Existing basin was built to handle a future impervious area.
A planting fund was set up for abutters at a past ground-mount solar project and suggested as a model.
The town has received traffic peer review fees; the applicant's attorney said engineering peer review would not be funded yet.

budget_items.topic: Mass Works infrastructure grants and MBTA Communities compliance
budget_items.what_was_said: Noncompliance could affect eligibility for certain state grants such as Mass Works.

decisions.decision: Board agreed to take up the municipal building concepts again at the next meeting in about two weeks.
Hearing to continue pending peer review comments and outcomes of other boards; applicant agreed to provide architectural renderings and truck turning templates.
Driveways and entrances bylaw review (section 250 6.4) deferred to the next meeting; staff to create a OneDrive folder for it.
Planner to send MBTA Communities action plan draft to members for discussion at next meeting; due end of month.
No pursuit of housing choice or Community Compact augmentation funds; members may bring ideas next meeting.

what_happened.line: The Planning Board continued the 1325 Mass Ave site plan and stormwater hearing to January 23 at 6:05 pm, 4-0 by roll call, after sharp abutter objections.
The hearing is waiting on peer review comments and the outcomes of other boards; the applicant agreed to provide architectural renderings and truck turning templates.
The board approved a modification to the Lunenburg Central site plan for signage, 4-0 by roll call, with existing conditions and none added.
The board endorsed an approval-not-required plan for 68 Laurel Lane, 4-0 by roll call.
The Select Board chair presented municipal building concepts with no vote; the Planning Board will take them up again in about two weeks.

why_it_matters: The 1325 Mass Ave project, a contractor storage building near the water supply district, is still undecided, and neighbors will have another chance to comment at the continued hearing.
The municipal building concepts, which weigh renovating against rebuilding, are likely to reach voters as a funding question, and early cost estimates were described as very large.
watch_next: The continued 1325 Mass Ave hearing on January 23 at 6:05 pm.
The MBTA Communities action plan draft, due at the end of the month, and the municipal building concepts at the next meeting.
